subject: Usage reallocation + eval credit request for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@bluelake.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage reallocation request + PO question

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Quick question ahead of our renewal: we ran a heavier-than-expected POC in June and overshot the non-prod commitment by ~45k token-hours. Our engineering team (cc'd internally) recommends we reallocate ~30% of our existing committed capacity from the non-prod SKU to the prod SKU for the next 12 months rather than increasing overall spend.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood accommodate a one-time reallocation of commit across SKUs within a renewal window (we were told private offers usually support this but wanted confirmation)?
- Given the POC overage, would Redwood consider a small eval credit to cover the overshoot while we finalize the PO?

I've attached our draft AWS Private Offer PO (BL_AWS_PO_Draft_v2.pdf) with the current SKU mapping. If we can split the commit 70/30 prod/non-prod and apply a one-time 10% credit against the overshoot, we should be able to proceed to signature by the end of next week.

Attached: BL_AWS_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 248KB)

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Cloud Ops
BlueLake Analytics
[sara@bluelake.ai]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@bluelake.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage reallocation request + PO question

Sara —

Appreciate the clear ask and the PO draft. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a commit reallocation inside a private offer at renewal, and we can typically grant a one-time eval/overshoot credit for POC bursts. I want to confirm two operational details so we can update the PO before you route it to procurement:

1) Commit split: we can map to two SKUs (PROD_SKU_A and NONPROD_SKU_B). Proposed split: 70% PROD_SKU_A / 30% NONPROD_SKU_B for a 12-month term. Ben — can you confirm throughput/latency parity for PROD_SKU_A at the bumped capacity?

2) Credit mechanics: we can apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of the overshoot tokens as a line-item credit on the first invoice after acceptance (DocuSign flow preferred). Kimberly — procurement/tax path: do we need an approved amendment or is a private-offer replacement sufficient for tax/invoice integrity?

If that's all good I will prepare a short amendment to the PO (no change to total committed $ if we only reallocate SKUs); if BlueLake wants to keep the dollar commitment identical we can just relabel usage buckets. Either way we should have a signed private offer ready by next Thursday if procurement has the invoice cadence.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm runtime profile for PROD_SKU_A (quick yes/no)
- Kimberly: confirm invoice cadence and whether we need an amendment doc or PO replacement
- Sara: if comfortable, route the PO back to me and I'll attach the commit-split worksheet we discussed.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
[Attachment referenced on our side: commit-split.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BL-2026-087 — SKUs + invoice mechanics (do not forward)

Kimberly/Ben — pulling threads together after Sara's note and our reply. Copying the core asks: commit reallocation (70/30 prod/non-prod) and a one-time 10% eval credit to cover the POC overshoot. BL has attached BL_AWS_PO_Draft_v2.pdf.

Operational suggestions:
- Split the commit into two line items on the PO: PROD_SKU_A (70%) and NONPROD_SKU_B (30%), same term length (12 months) so we avoid a new procurement review. We'll keep the total committed $ static; it's a reallocation, not an uplift.
- Apply a one-time credit line ("PO Credit: POC Overshoot") that nets against the first invoice after acceptance. Finance prefers a single invoice adjustment rather than ongoing pro-ration.
- Procurement needs explicit invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and the legal team needs the revised PO PDF for signature. If we replace the existing private offer on the marketplace we must ensure the DocuSign envelope references the correct HubSpot deal id (HSP-4321).

I've sketched the commit-split in the attached spreadsheet (commit-split.xlsx) with exact token-hour numbers by SKU so we can generate the line items. Ben — can you confirm that the PROD_SKU_A performance profile supports the 70% increase without needing a reserved throughput SLA change? If so we'll proceed with a marketplace private-offer replacement and route the DocuSign link to BlueLake.

Notes on tax/billing: Kimberley — they are US-based (CA billing address) so we need VAT/withholding not applicable, but state tax info required on the invoice. Procurement has asked to receive the invoice quarterly if possible.

Please confirm quickly — Sara is hoping to sign by next Thursday.

[Attachment: commit-split.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12KB)]

—Avery

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: BL-2026-087 — SKUs + invoice mechanics (do not forward)

Thanks Avery — quick confirmations:

- Invoice cadence: quarterly invoices are fine. We'll include a one-line credit against the first quarter invoice (PO Credit: POC Overshoot). Finance will process that as a negative line item.
- Doc flow: because this is a commit reallocation (no net increase in contracted $) we can issue a replacement private offer on the AWS marketplace and reference the same HubSpot deal (HSP-4321). Legal prefers replacement rather than an amendment to keep the marketplace acceptance path clean.
- Tax info: BlueLake will need us to include our US tax ID and their CA tax nexus on the invoice; ask them to confirm the billing address exactly as it should appear.

Ben — please send a quick technical sign-off (1-2 lines) confirming PROD_SKU_A handles the bumped steady-state. If yes I will prepare the replacement PO PDF and coordinate DocuSign.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@bluelake.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueLake Billing <billing@bluelake.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage reallocation request + PO question — confirmed

Avery/Kimberly — thanks for the fast turnaround. BlueLake approves the proposed approach: 70% PROD_SKU_A / 30% NONPROD_SKU_B, quarterly invoice cadence, and the one-time 10% credit on the first invoice.

We'll confirm billing address and CA tax details to Kimberly separately (billing@bluelake.ai). Please proceed with the replacement private offer on AWS and send the DocuSign link — I'll route to our procurement manager for signature once the updated PO is attached.

Expected next steps from Redwood:
1) Replacement private offer PDF (with split line items) uploaded to DocuSign and link shared.
2) HubSpot deal HSP-4321 updated with final PO and DocuSign envelope id.
3) One-time credit applied to first quarter invoice after acceptance.

I'll confirm signature timeline after procurement reviews the updated PO (should be within 48 hours). Appreciate you accommodating the reallocation — this keeps us within the same overall commit and avoids an immediate uplift.

Best,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Cloud Ops
BlueLake Analytics
sara@bluelake.ai
